This index captures the degree of folding or compactness of a network, and is related to subgraph centrality and the number of closed walks. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The Estrada index. Returns 0.0 for empty graphs, 1.0 for single-node graphs. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is directed (Estrada index is only defined for undirected graphs). ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} The Estrada index $EE(G) = \sum_i e^{\lambda_i} = \mathrm{tr}(e^A)$ (Estrada, 2000) is the trace of the matrix exponential of the adjacency matrix, and Taylor-expanding $e^A$ shows that it counts closed walks of every length weighted by $1/k!$: so it grows whenever a graph carries more short closed walks (triangles, tetrahedra, and higher cliques). Because $EE = n$ for the edgeless graph and increases with every additional walk, it always satisfies $EE(G) \ge n$. It is tightly connected to the *subgraph centrality*: node $i$'s score $SC(i) = \sum_j \phi_j(i)^2 e^{\lambda_j}$ is the $i$-th diagonal entry of $e^A$, so $EE = \sum_i SC(i)$. Computation costs $O(n^3)$ via dense eigendecomposition of $A$; only undirected inputs are supported since the definition assumes a real symmetric spectrum. ## Examples {.doc-examples} A single edge (`K_2`) has eigenvalues `1` and `-1`, so its Estrada index is `exp(1) + exp(-1) ≈ 3.086`: ::: {#a940aef3 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph() g.add_node(label="A") g.add_node(label="B") g.add_edge("A", "B") # Returns approximately 3.086 g.estrada_index() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 3.0861612696304874 ``` ::: ::: A graph with no edges at all has every eigenvalue equal to zero, so its Estrada index always equals the number of nodes: ::: {#5e4c768d .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} isolated = ec.Graph() for i in range(5): isolated.add_node() # Returns 5.0 isolated.estrada_index() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 5.0 ``` ::: :::
